literary_histories.consulted_argument: Andrew C. Witt, Journal for the Evangelical Study of the Old Testament 3.1 (2014), 77–97; root read displayed comparison/argument pp.85–97, not native PDF
live_options: Qumran Hebrew expansion of a shorter predecessor
Separate development from shared lost predecessor
literary_histories.strong_countercase: Witt argues expansion from framing and community vocabulary; coherent framing could also be abbreviated and compatible vocabulary alone does not establish chronology

literary_histories.outcome: No unique exact Greek Vorlage or earliest literary form established

oil_mercy_unit.alternative: ἐλέει; mercy, as reported for ℵAR

oil_mercy_unit.support_for_oil: Declared selected Greek text and explicit holy oil in related Hebrew 151A; natural anointing context
oil_mercy_unit.strong_countercase: Substantial reported Greek support for mercy; oil could be contextual normalization. Related Hebrew literary form does not independently settle Greek priority

oil_mercy_unit.decision: Retain selected oil provisionally, hold historical priority; no source/main-English change
oil_mercy_unit.discriminating_next_evidence: Modern passage apparatus and hand-separated Greek collation; R Psalm 151 must be dated as its later addition, not host codex
